overview.problem: Eight independently confirmed findings sit in the traktor_nml package. Three are correctness gaps where a command skips a convention the older write commands already enforce: rewrite-from-collection-compare accepts an output equal to the newer collection and matches without the one-to-one destination-collision guarantee DL-004 states, and split lets a playlist outside the current group decide that group dangling-reference outcome. One is a silently dead feature: the fingerprint tier builds an old-side path from a volume-relative decoded_path, so the file is never found and the tier contributes nothing on the side it exists for. Two are safety gaps in splice and split: a malformed input escapes as a parser exception rather than the documented diagnostic, and outputs are written with a truncating write. Two are quadratic scans over document size, in spans.element_span_by_identity and playlists._locate_node_start, both called once per entry or node on an 11.7MB, 6412-entry real corpus.
overview.approach: Each fix routes the offending command through the mechanism the package already owns for that concern rather than adding a local patch beside it. The destination-collision post-pass becomes a named function in reconnect.py that both the reconnect path and the compare path call. volumes.py gains the documented inverse of location_from_disk_path and the fingerprint tier uses it. splice and split read, parse and write through helpers lifted out of rewrite.py so they inherit write_nml_safely diagnostics and its atomic write. spans.py gains one SpanIndex built in a single pass per document, and it replaces both quadratic locators, leaving one element-to-span strategy. Every fix lands with a test that fails without it, since each finding exists because no test covered its trigger.

decisions.decision: One SpanIndex, built in a single pass per source document, is the only mechanism that maps a parsed element to its source byte span
decisions.reasoning: element_span already scans forward once from a known offset and is linear over the element extent, while element_span_by_identity re-walks root.iter(tag) and re-scans source from offset zero on every call and playlists._locate_node_start runs find plus rfind over the whole document per playlist node -> on the 6412-entry 11.7MB corpus both are quadratic over document size because split and splice call them once per surviving entry and per playlist node -> a single pre-order walk assigning each element its per-tag ordinal plus a single _TOKEN_RE.finditer pass collecting per-tag opening-tag offsets answers every lookup in constant time, matches the single-pass discipline element_span already documents (existing DL-007, byte-span assembly), and leaves exactly one indexing strategy in the package

decisions.decision: The destination-collision post-pass lives in reconnect.py as a named function that both resolve_reconnection and compare-based rewriting call, rather than being duplicated inside compare_cmd
decisions.reasoning: The repository's existing DL-004 (reconnect.py's one-to-one assignment guarantee, README Invariants) is enforced as a post-match inversion over match_records output, and reconnect.py is today its only caller -> compare-based rewriting calls match_records directly, so two old collection entries that each match one new entry unambiguously both get rewritten onto one LOCATION and one PRIMARYKEY, the exact outcome existing DL-004 forbids -> lifting the inversion into a shared function keeps one implementation of that existing invariant, lets compare keep the sample list match_records returns (which resolve_reconnection discards), and keeps reconnect.py the owner of the invariant its own docstring documents

decisions.decision: The compare-based rewrite stats gain destination_collisions and the baselines manifest case for rewrite-from-collection-compare is regenerated
decisions.reasoning: Enforcing existing DL-004's one-to-one rule on the compare path withdraws collided matches and changes the matched total -> a withdrawal that is not reported leaves the operator unable to tell a genuinely unmatched track from a withdrawn one, which is why the reconnect path already prints the counter -> printing the same counter on the compare path changes recorded stdout for one manifest case, and manifest.schema.md sanctions regeneration for a deliberate reviewed behavior change, so the manifest is regenerated with the change recorded rather than the counter being suppressed to protect a byte-identical baseline

decisions.decision: volumes.py owns a documented inverse of location_from_disk_path that turns a collection LOCATION back into an absolute on-disk path, and fingerprint.py uses it for the old side
decisions.reasoning: decoded_path is volume-relative by design because VOLUME and VOLUMEID are separate fields, so Path(str(record.location.decoded_path)) names a path rooted at the filesystem root rather than at the volume -> old_side_fingerprint therefore fails is_file for essentially every real record and the fingerprint tier is silently dead on the old side while its unavailable counter absorbs the failure -> reattaching volume identity is exactly the inverse of the transformation volumes.py and reconnect.location_from_disk_path already own for the candidate side, so the inverse belongs beside them, is testable as a round trip rather than as a fingerprint run, and keeps every piece of volume reasoning in the module the existing DL-005 governs

decisions.decision: local_path_for_location resolves only against mount anchors already established for the record's own VOLUME/VOLUMEID by resolve_volume_identity or --volume-map; an unknown volume, or two known anchors that both resolve, yields None rather than a guessed path
decisions.reasoning: The repository's existing DL-005 (volumes.py docstring, README Invariants) states that volume identity is explicit and never inferred from the stale decoded paths reconnection exists to repair, permitting inference only where a prefix scan yields exactly one distinct VOLUME/VOLUMEID pair and hard-erroring otherwise -> probing an ordered list of plausible anchors (a drive designator read out of the VOLUME string, a POSIX mount directory named after it, the filesystem root) and accepting the first that is_file-resolves is exactly the path-based guessing existing DL-005 forbids, and its failure mode is a false positive: a different file that happens to sit at the same volume-relative path under the wrong anchor is fingerprinted and can win a match that rewrites LOCATION and PRIMARYKEY onto an unrelated track -> the resolver instead takes a mounts mapping from (VOLUME, VOLUMEID) to the mount anchors this run has already established explicitly (each --volume-map entry and each --scan-root whose identity resolve_volume_identity resolved, anchored the same way resolve_volume_identity's own prefix comparison anchors them), returns the resolved path only when exactly one known anchor yields a readable file, and returns None for an unknown volume or for two anchors that disagree, so the old-side lookup inherits existing DL-005's explicitness instead of carving an exception out of it

decisions.decision: splice_cmd and split_cmd read, parse and write through helpers exported from rewrite.py instead of carrying their own input handling and plain write_bytes
decisions.reasoning: write_nml_safely already encodes the tool conventions for a write command, namely refusing output equal to any input, reporting a parse failure as xml_parse_error with exit code 2, and writing through a temp file plus os.replace -> splice and split reproduce only part of that, so a malformed input raises an lxml exception out of the handler instead of the documented diagnostic, and an interrupted write truncates a destination that previously held a valid collection -> exposing the read-and-parse step and the atomic write from rewrite.py as named helpers gives the span-transplantation commands the same guarantees without forcing their multi-input, multi-output shape through write_nml_safely, whose single-input single-output patch-and-write skeleton does not fit them

decisions.decision: apply_dangling_policy inspects only the playlists the current group names, not every playlist in the document
decisions.reasoning: build_output produces one output per group and the policy decides that output alone -> scanning every playlist node in the file lets an untouched playlist elsewhere in the document decide this group, so pull-in drags in tracks no requested playlist references and fail aborts a group whose own playlists are entirely sound -> passing the resolved group nodes into the policy makes each output depend only on its own selection, which is what the repository's existing DL-009 (split.py's named-playlist selection and per-output dangling semantics) describes

decisions.decision: playlists.py locates an imported node through SpanIndex and its UUID-based locator is removed
decisions.reasoning: _locate_node_start finds the PLAYLIST child UUID and then searches backwards for the enclosing NODE open tag, which is a second, weaker way of answering the question the identity locator answers -> it is also the slower of the two, scanning the whole document per node, and it fails outright on a playlist whose PLAYLIST child carries no UUID (the regenerated-UUID risk the existing DL-008 already records) -> routing it through the same SpanIndex the collection entries use removes the duplicate mechanism along with the rescan

decisions.decision: Per-file temp-plus-os.replace atomicity is added underneath the existing DL-012 build-and-validate-before-write rule, and split's multi-output write loop stays non-transactional across files by explicit choice
decisions.reasoning: The repository's existing DL-012 invariant is that a write command builds its complete output in memory and validates it before any file handle opens, which split_cmd already satisfies by assembling and checking every group before its write loop starts -> that covers computation-phase failure but not write-phase failure: a disk error on the third of four group outputs still leaves the first two written, and a truncating write_bytes can additionally leave one destination half-written -> adding temp-plus-os.replace makes each individual destination hold either its previous bytes or the complete new bytes, closing the truncation hole existing DL-012 never addressed, while cross-file rollback of already-replaced outputs would need a staging-and-commit protocol that is new machinery beyond a fix-only pass, so the residual gap is recorded as a bounded tradeoff rather than silently implied to be closed

decisions.decision: write_nml_safely's output-equals-input refusal covers every file a command reads in that invocation, not only its primary input, and compare-based rewriting declares new_input through extra_inputs
decisions.reasoning: write_nml_safely already owns the refusal and already accepts extra_inputs precisely so a command reading more than one file can declare the rest -> rewrite-from-collection-compare reads two collections but declares only old_input, so an output that resolves to new_input is accepted and the newer collection is overwritten in place by a rewrite derived from it, destroying the very file the run compared against, even though the same command already refuses the identical mistake against old_input -> stating the rule generally as 'a write command refuses an output path that resolves to any of its inputs' and requiring every multi-input command to declare its remaining inputs through extra_inputs closes the gap as a convention future multi-input commands are checked against, rather than as a one-line special case at a single call site

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Memoize element_span_by_identity and _locate_node_start behind per-call caches, keeping both locators
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Leaves two element-to-span mechanisms plus a third caching layer, and the tree walk inside element_span_by_identity stays linear per call, so the quadratic term survives for documents with many same-tag elements

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Call reconnect.resolve_reconnection directly from compare-based rewriting
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: resolve_reconnection discards the sample list compare prints and produces ambiguity rows compare has no CSV surface for; the shared piece is the collision post-pass, not the whole reconnection wrapper

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Suppress the destination_collisions counter on the compare path so the recorded baseline stdout stays byte-identical
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: A withdrawn match that is not reported is indistinguishable from an unmatched track, which is why the reconnect path prints it; manifest.schema.md provides regeneration for exactly this case

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Probe an ordered list of plausible mount anchors for the old-side path (a drive designator parsed out of the VOLUME string, a POSIX mount directory named after it, the filesystem root) and accept the first that resolves to a readable file
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: The is_file probe cannot tell the record's own file from a different file sitting at the same volume-relative path under the wrong anchor, and the filesystem-root candidate reproduces today's buggy construction exactly; a wrong resolution is fingerprinted and can win a match that rewrites LOCATION and PRIMARYKEY onto an unrelated track, which is precisely the path-based inference the existing DL-005 forbids

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Route splice and split through write_nml_safely itself
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: That helper is a single-input, single-output parse-patch-write skeleton with an lxml and a stdlib branch; splice merges several inputs and split emits several outputs from one fully assembled string, so the fit would distort the helper rather than share it

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Add a CLI flag mapping a VOLUME value to its mount point for old-side fingerprinting
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: New CLI surface is out of scope for a fix-only pass, and --volume-map plus the resolved --scan-root identities already give the run an explicit, existing-DL-005-sanctioned source of mount anchors for exactly the volumes this run touches

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Stage every split group output to a temp file and commit them together so a mid-loop failure rolls back the outputs already written
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: A cross-file commit protocol is new machinery well past a fix-only pass; the finding under repair is the truncating single-file write, which temp-plus-os.replace closes, and the residual cross-file gap is recorded as a tradeoff under DL-022 instead of being closed silently

constraints: MUST: no previously-passing test regresses. The pass condition is that pytest tests/ -q from C:/codex/general_tasks reports zero failures and zero errors, and that every test which passed before a milestone still passes after it. Test counts are deliberately not a pass condition: every milestone adds tests, so the totals are expected to grow. '42 passed, 2 skipped' is recorded only as a dated reference baseline from the pre-fix run (2026-08-23) for identifying which tests pre-existed, never as a count to match

Byte-preserving write invariants hold: the attribute-patch path through write_nml_safely and the span-transplantation path through OutputBuilder and spans.py both keep every untouched byte of the source
Each fixed finding is covered by a test that exercises the previously uncaught trigger condition
The efficiency fixes use one single-pass precomputation consistent with spans.element_span, not a third indexing strategy
Fix-only scope: no new features, no new CLI surface, no broader refactor beyond what the eight findings require

risks.risk: Enforcing one-to-one on the compare path changes recorded stdout for one baseline manifest case
risks.mitigation: Regenerate that case through tests/baselines/regenerate.py rather than hand-editing the manifest, and gate the regeneration on an explicit scope check performed by the milestone's own acceptance criterion: the implementer diffs the regenerated manifest against the committed one and the diff must consist solely of the added destination_collisions counter line in the rewrite-from-collection-compare case, with any other changed byte in any other case treated as a regression to investigate before the regenerated manifest is accepted; test_baseline_parity only proves the manifest matches current behavior, so it cannot substitute for that scope check

risks.risk: SpanIndex ordinal assignment assumes the parser pre-order over the tree matches left-to-right opening-tag order in source, the same assumption element_span_by_identity documents
risks.mitigation: Assert index spans equal element_span results for every ENTRY and NODE across the real fixture, including nested same-named and self-closing elements

risks.risk: Old-side volume resolution is limited to mount anchors this run established explicitly, so a record on a volume neither --volume-map nor any --scan-root identifies still fails to resolve
risks.mitigation: The unresolved case keeps counting fingerprint_unavailable_old_side, so the tier degrades exactly as it does for a genuinely absent file; this is a false negative (a fingerprint not taken) and is preferred over the false positive R-005 describes

risks.risk: Scoping the dangling policy to a group narrows what pull-in and fail see, which changes outcomes for callers relying on the whole-document behavior
risks.mitigation: The whole-document behavior contradicts the existing DL-009 per-output semantics; existing exclude and fail expectations for references held by requested playlists stay asserted unchanged

risks.risk: A wrong resolution on the old side is worse than no resolution: if local_path_for_location returned a different file that happens to sit at the same volume-relative path under another anchor, that file's fingerprint could win a match and rewrite LOCATION and PRIMARYKEY onto an unrelated track, and nothing downstream would flag it
risks.mitigation: The resolver never guesses an anchor: it consults only the (VOLUME, VOLUMEID) to mount-anchor mapping built from --volume-map entries and from scan roots whose identity resolve_volume_identity resolved, it drops the filesystem-root candidate entirely, and it returns None when a record's pair is unknown or when two known anchors both yield a readable file, so an ambiguous case degrades to fingerprint_unavailable_old_side instead of silently picking one. A test asserts the wrong-anchor case directly: the same volume-relative path is populated with a different file under a second, unmapped anchor and the resolver must return None rather than that file. This keeps the existing DL-005 rule (volume identity is explicit, never inferred from stale paths) intact rather than carving an old-side exception out of it

invisible_knowledge.system: Two write mechanisms coexist and never mix within one command. The attribute-patch path (textpatch.py driven by rewrite.py and reconnect.py) substitutes attribute values inside opening tags located in raw source text, and rewrite.write_nml_safely carries its conventions: refuse an output equal to any input, report a parse failure as xml_parse_error with exit code 2, and write through a temp file plus os.replace. The span-transplantation path (spans.py driven by splice.py and split.py) concatenates verbatim source byte ranges. All eight findings are cases where the newer commands on the second path, plus compare-based rewriting, do not inherit a convention the first path already implements correctly; the fixes make the conventions shared rather than reimplementing them per command.
invariants: A candidate matched by more than one old record is withdrawn from every mapping the tool writes from, on both the reconnect and the compare path, and the withdrawal is counted (extends the existing DL-004 guarantee to the compare path)
A write command refuses an output path that resolves to any of its inputs
A malformed input yields xml_parse_error naming the file and exit code 2, never an escaping parser exception

Every output file is written through a temp file plus os.replace, so a destination holds either its previous content or the complete new content; this sits underneath the existing DL-012 build-and-validate-before-write rule and does not extend to rolling back sibling outputs already replaced in a multi-output run
An element is located in source by tree identity through one SpanIndex per document, never by searching for an attribute value and never by a second locator
A split output depends only on the playlists its own group names

An old-side path is reconstructed by reattaching volume identity to the volume-relative decoded path, never by treating decoded_path as absolute and never by guessing a mount anchor the run has not explicitly established
tradeoffs: Reporting destination_collisions on the compare path costs one regenerated baseline case, accepted so a withdrawn match stays visible

Old-side volume resolution is confined to mount anchors the run established explicitly, so a record on an unmapped volume is simply not fingerprinted, accepted because a guessed anchor risks fingerprinting the wrong file and rewriting a track onto an unrelated location
SpanIndex holds per-tag offset lists for the whole document in memory, accepted because the alternative is a document rescan per element on an 11.7MB corpus

split's multi-output write loop stays non-transactional across files: each destination is individually atomic, but a failure partway through the loop leaves earlier groups written, accepted because cross-file staging and commit is new machinery beyond a fix-only pass

milestones.name: Old-side path resolution for the fingerprint tier
requirements: A collection LOCATION resolves back to the absolute on-disk path it was encoded from; old_side_fingerprint fingerprints a record whose recorded file is present on a mounted volume; a record whose volume is absent counts as fingerprint_unavailable_old_side
acceptance_criteria: A round-trip test asserts local_path_for_location of location_from_disk_path for a real file under tmp_path, with that file's volume identity present in the known-mounts mapping, returns that same file

old_side_fingerprint on a record whose VOLUME/VOLUMEID pair is in no known mount increments fingerprint_unavailable_old_side and returns nothing
local_path_for_location returns None, not a path, when a file with the same volume-relative path exists under an anchor that is not a known mount for that record's pair
local_path_for_location returns None when two known anchors for one pair both yield a readable file
README.md Design Decisions and Invariants carry DL-017 and DL-018 and state that old-side resolution never guesses an anchor, and both CLAUDE.md indexes describe volumes.py's new public function
No previously-passing test regresses (pytest tests/ -q)
tests: type: integration plus round-trip property assertion, in tests/test_fingerprint.py
backing: doc-derived from the existing DL-005 explicit-identity rule
normal: a LOCATION whose pair is a known mount resolves to the file on disk
edge: a LOCATION whose DIR is the volume root; two known anchors both holding a file at that relative path
error: a LOCATION whose pair is in no known mount, and a decoy file at the same relative path under an unmapped anchor - both must resolve to None rather than to the decoy

code_intents.behavior: Turn a LocationParts back into the absolute on-disk path it names, inverting location_from_disk_path. The function takes the location together with a mapping from (VOLUME, VOLUMEID) to the mount anchors this run has established explicitly, joins the decoded volume-relative path onto each anchor recorded for that record's own pair, and returns the resolved path only when exactly one such candidate is a readable file. It returns None when the pair appears in no mapping, when no candidate resolves, and when two distinct anchors for one pair both resolve. It never parses an anchor out of the VOLUME string, never derives one from a POSIX mount-directory convention, and never falls back to the filesystem root, because those are inferences from the same stale decoded paths the existing DL-005 rules out and their failure mode is a wrong file rather than a missing one. Volume identity resolution stays in this module beside resolve_volume_identity and location_from_disk_path so both directions of the transformation, and the single explicitness rule governing them, are described in one place.

Resolve the record's recorded location through local_path_for_location, passing the known-mounts mapping the caller supplies, instead of constructing a Path from the volume-relative decoded_path, and count fingerprint_unavailable_old_side when the resolver yields nothing - which now covers the unknown-volume and ambiguous-anchor cases as well as a genuinely missing file. fingerprint_key_provider gains the mapping as a parameter and threads it through. The docstring names volume reattachment as the reason the old side needs a resolver at all, and states that an unresolvable or ambiguous volume is deliberately counted as unavailable rather than guessed.

Round-trip a real file under tmp_path through location_from_disk_path and back through local_path_for_location with that file's volume identity registered as a known mount, and assert equality; assert old_side_fingerprint on that record leaves fingerprint_unavailable_old_side at zero for the path step while a record whose pair is in no known mount increments it; assert the wrong-resolution case directly by writing a different file at the same volume-relative path under a second anchor that is not a known mount for that pair and asserting the resolver returns None rather than the decoy, and by registering two anchors for one pair that both hold a file and asserting None again. The round trip is the assertion because it holds without pyacoustid installed, unlike a real fingerprint comparison.

Resolve the scan-root volume identities before the key providers are constructed rather than after matching, and build from them plus the parsed --volume-map a mapping from (VOLUME, VOLUMEID) to mount anchors, anchoring each scan root the same way resolve_volume_identity's own prefix comparison does. Pass that mapping into fingerprint_key_provider so the old side resolves against identities this run established explicitly, and keep using the same resolved identities for the existing candidate-side re-encoding so there is one resolution step, not two.

Add, in the existing (DL-nnn) citation style, that volumes.py owns both directions of the volume-relative to absolute transformation and that the old-side inverse resolves only against mount anchors the run established explicitly, returning nothing for an unknown pair or two anchors that both resolve, because a guessed anchor can fingerprint a different file and rewrite a track onto an unrelated location (DL-017, DL-018) - stated as an extension of the existing DL-005 explicit-identity invariant already recorded there, not an exception to it.

Update the volumes.py row to name local_path_for_location alongside resolve_volume_identity and location_from_disk_path, and the fingerprint.py row to say the old side resolves its path through volumes.py rather than from decoded_path, so the navigation index still describes what those modules do.
Update the reconnect_cmd.py row to note that volume identities are resolved before key providers are built and supplied to the fingerprint provider as the old side's known-mounts mapping.

error: interruption is injected by monkeypatching os.replace in the traktor_nml.rewrite namespace to raise OSError when the destination under test is committed, with the pre-existing destination bytes captured before the run and asserted unchanged after it, plus an assertion that the temp file the helper created no longer exists - the raise-at-commit point is what makes the test able to fail, since asserting on an uninterrupted run would pass against a truncating write too

code_intents.behavior: Read and parse the base and every --input contribution through rewrite.read_and_parse_source so a malformed file yields xml_parse_error naming that file and exit code 2 instead of an lxml exception escaping the handler, and write the assembled output through rewrite.write_bytes_atomically so an interrupted write cannot truncate an existing destination.

The comment at the write loop states what the per-file atomicity does and does not buy: each destination holds either its previous bytes or the complete new bytes, but a failure partway through the loop still leaves earlier groups written, which is the bounded tradeoff DL-022 records rather than an oversight.

+class SpanIndex:
+    """Index one source document against its parsed root in a single pass,
+    so every element in the tree resolves to its byte span without
+    rescanning the source per lookup.
+
+    One pre-order walk (root.iter()) assigns every element its ordinal
+    among same-tag elements, in the same left-to-right order a well-formed
+    document's own opening tags appear in source; one _TOKEN_RE scan then
+    collects the opening-tag offset of every non-closing tag occurrence in
+    document order. span_of resolves an element's offset by tag and
+    ordinal and returns element_span from there.
+
+    The same walk that assigns ordinals also keeps a reference to every
+    walked element for this index's entire lifetime (self._elements). This
+    matters specifically under the lxml backend: an lxml Element is a
+    transient proxy over the underlying libxml2 tree, and once nothing
+    references a proxy it can be garbage-collected - after which CPython
+    may reuse its memory address for a brand-new, unrelated proxy object.
+    Keying solely on id(element) without retaining a reference would let a
+    later, different element be assigned the same id() as an
+    already-collected one, and span_of would then silently resolve to the
+    wrong (stale) ordinal for that address. Holding self._elements for as
+    long as this index is alive guarantees every id() this index has ever
+    recorded stays bound to the original element for the index's whole
+    lifetime, so a lookup can never be confused by address reuse.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, source: str, root) -> None:
+        self._source = source
+        self._elements: list = []
+        self._ordinal_by_id: dict[int, int] = {}
+        tag_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
+        for element in root.iter():
+            tag = element.tag
+            if not isinstance(tag, str):
+                continue  # skip comments/PIs, whose lxml .tag is a callable, not a name
+            self._elements.append(element)
+            ordinal = tag_counts.get(tag, 0)
+            self._ordinal_by_id[id(element)] = ordinal
+            tag_counts[tag] = ordinal + 1
+
+        offsets_by_tag: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
+        for token in _TOKEN_RE.finditer(source):
+            if token.group(1):  # a closing tag never starts a new element
+                continue
+            tag_name = token.group(2)
+            if tag_name is None:
+                continue
+            offsets_by_tag.setdefault(tag_name, []).append(token.start())
+        self._offsets_by_tag = offsets_by_tag
+
+    def span_of(self, element) -> Span:
+        """Return element's full byte span, resolved by its tag and
+        ordinal among same-tag elements rather than by rescanning source.
+        Raises ValueError naming the tag when element is absent from the
+        indexed tree, or when that tag's source occurrences run short of
+        its ordinal."""
+        tag_name = element.tag
+        ordinal = self._ordinal_by_id.get(id(element))
+        if ordinal is None:
+            raise ValueError(f"element <{tag_name}> is not part of the indexed tree")
+        offsets = self._offsets_by_tag.get(tag_name, [])
+        if ordinal >= len(offsets):
+            raise ValueError(f"could not locate occurrence {ordinal} of <{tag_name}> in source text")
+        return element_span(self._source, offsets[ordinal])
+

No previously-passing test regresses (pytest tests/ -q)
tests: type: integration through run_tool, in tests/test_split.py, plus the spans unit tests for the removed locator
backing: doc-derived from the repository's existing DL-009 (split.py's named-playlist selection and per-output dangling semantics), not from any decision introduced by this plan
normal: exclude drops an out-of-selection reference held by a requested playlist
edge: pull-in with a broken reference in an unrequested playlist
error: fail triggered only by a requested playlist

code_intents.behavior: Take the playlist nodes the current group resolved to, rather than the whole document, and apply the exclude, pull-in and fail policy over only their PRIMARYKEY references, so each output depends on its own selection alone. select_entries hands over the resolved nodes it already looked up so neither function searches the document twice.

Accept the SpanIndex for the source document and use it for kept collection entries, retained playlist nodes and carried-over SORTING_INFO entries, replacing all three element_span_by_identity call sites, so a group is assembled without rescanning the source per entry, and pass the resolved group nodes into apply_dangling_policy.

Assert a group whose own playlists are sound succeeds under --dangling-policy fail while an unrequested playlist in the same file holds a broken reference; assert --dangling-policy pull-in adds no track that only an unrequested playlist references; keep the existing exclude and fail expectations for references held by requested playlists.

Remove the function and its export now that split.py, its last caller, resolves spans through SpanIndex, leaving exactly one element-to-span mechanism in the package. The removal happens here rather than in M-004 because M-004 runs in the earlier wave and split.py is migrated in this one; deleting it earlier would leave a shipped module importing a name that no longer exists and the suite red at the wave boundary.

Build one SpanIndex for the parsed source and pass it to build_output on every group iteration, updating the call site to the new signature so the index is built once per document rather than once per group, and keep the existing build-all-then-write-all ordering intact.
Drop or re-point the tests that exercised element_span_by_identity directly onto SpanIndex, so removing the function does not silently delete coverage of the identity-location behavior it provided.

Record that a split output depends only on the playlists its own group names, so an untouched playlist elsewhere in the document can neither pull tracks into a group nor fail it, stated as what the existing DL-009 per-output semantics already imply (DL-020).

Update the split.py row to say the dangling policy is scoped to the group's own resolved playlist nodes and that spans come from the shared SpanIndex, and confirm the spans.py row no longer names element_span_by_identity.
Update the split_cmd.py row to say one SpanIndex is built per input and handed to build_output for every group.

readme_entries.content:
Additions for traktor_nml/README.md, in the file's existing (DL-nnn)
citation style. New decisions continue the repository's existing decision
log, which already occupies DL-001..DL-013, so they begin at DL-014; every
reference to a pre-existing decision below names it as such.

## Design Decisions (append)

- `spans.py` builds one `SpanIndex` per source document in a single pass -
  one pre-order walk for per-tag ordinals, one token scan for opening-tag
  offsets - and it is the only mechanism that maps a parsed element to its
  source byte span. `element_span_by_identity` and `playlists.py`'s
  UUID-marker locator are both gone, so a playlist whose `PLAYLIST` child
  carries no UUID is still located and no locator rescans the document per
  element (DL-014, DL-021).
- The one-to-one destination-collision post-pass is a named function in
  `reconnect.py` that both `resolve_reconnection` and compare-based
  rewriting call, so the pre-existing DL-004 guarantee has one
  implementation rather than one per caller (DL-015).
- `write_nml_safely`'s output-equals-input refusal is stated over every
  file the invocation reads, not only its primary input: a command with
  more than one input declares the rest through `extra_inputs`.
  `rewrite-from-collection-compare` reads two collections and declares
  `new_input`, so an output resolving to the newer collection is refused
  the same way one resolving to `old_input` already was (DL-023).
- `volumes.py` owns both directions of the volume-relative to absolute
  transformation: `location_from_disk_path` for the candidate side and
  `local_path_for_location` for the old side (DL-017).
- `local_path_for_location` resolves only against mount anchors this run
  established explicitly - `--volume-map` entries and scan roots whose
  identity `resolve_volume_identity` resolved - and returns nothing for an
  unknown VOLUME/VOLUMEID pair or for two known anchors that both yield a
  readable file. It never parses an anchor out of the VOLUME string and
  never falls back to the filesystem root: a guessed anchor can resolve to
  a different file sitting at the same volume-relative path, whose
  fingerprint could then win a match and rewrite LOCATION and PRIMARYKEY
  onto an unrelated track. This extends the pre-existing DL-005
  explicit-identity rule to the old side rather than carving an exception
  out of it (DL-018).
- `splice_cmd` and `split_cmd` read, parse and write through helpers
  exported from `rewrite.py` rather than carrying their own input handling
  and a plain `write_bytes`, so both inherit the diagnostics and the atomic
  write `write_nml_safely` already implements (DL-019).

## Invariants (append)

- A candidate matched by more than one old record is withdrawn from every
  mapping the tool writes from, on the compare path as well as the
  reconnect path, and the withdrawal is reported as `destination_collisions`
  (pre-existing DL-004, extended by DL-015 and DL-016).
- A write command refuses an output path that resolves to any of its
  inputs, not only its primary one; a multi-input command declares its
  remaining inputs through `write_nml_safely`'s `extra_inputs` (DL-023).
- A malformed input yields `xml_parse_error` naming the file and exit code
  2 from every write command, splice and split included, never an escaping
  parser exception (DL-019).
- Every output file is committed through a temp file plus `os.replace`, so
  a destination holds either its previous bytes or the complete new bytes.
  This sits underneath the pre-existing DL-012 build-and-validate-before-write
  rule and closes the truncation hole that rule never covered (DL-019).
- An element is located in source by tree identity through one `SpanIndex`
  per document, never by searching for an attribute value and never by a
  second locator (DL-014, DL-021).
- A split output depends only on the playlists its own group names: an
  untouched playlist elsewhere in the document can neither pull tracks into
  a group under `pull-in` nor abort it under `fail`, which is what the
  pre-existing DL-009 per-output semantics already imply (DL-020).
- An old-side path is reconstructed by reattaching volume identity to the
  volume-relative decoded path, never by treating `decoded_path` as
  absolute and never by guessing a mount anchor (DL-017, DL-018).

## Tradeoffs (append)

- Reporting `destination_collisions` on the compare path costs one
  regenerated baseline manifest case; accepted so a withdrawn match stays
  distinguishable from a genuinely unmatched track (DL-016).
- Old-side volume resolution is confined to explicitly established mount
  anchors, so a record on an unmapped volume is simply not fingerprinted
  and counts as `fingerprint_unavailable_old_side`; accepted because the
  alternative failure mode is fingerprinting the wrong file (DL-018).
- `SpanIndex` holds per-tag offset lists for the whole document in memory;
  accepted because the alternative is a document rescan per element on an
  11.7MB, 6412-entry corpus (DL-014).
- `split`'s multi-output write loop is not transactional across files: each
  destination is individually atomic, but a failure partway through the
  loop leaves earlier group outputs written. Accepted because cross-file
  staging and commit is new machinery beyond a fix-only pass, and recorded
  here rather than left implied by the per-file atomicity claim (DL-022).
